audit_findings.title: Historical OE record appears irreconcilable with audited cash flows
audit_findings.magnitude: $351.3 million FY2025 gap: supplied OE of -$210.5 million versus $140.8 million computed from filed net income plus D&A less vessel capital expenditures
audit_findings.mechanism: Historical OE errors control the trend-versus-latest anchor rule, the too-hard determination, and scenario growth assumptions.
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash provided by operating activities for the year ended March 31, 2026 was $210.1 million compared with $173.0 million for the year ended March 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated inconsistency, although the exact corrected OE series remains unresolved. The FY2025 filing reports $90.2 million of net income, $69.6 million of D&A, and $18.9 million of vessel capital expenditures, producing positive $140.8 million under the same construction that reproduces the FY2026 anchor—not negative $210.5 million. Filed operating cash flow less vessel capital expenditures is also positive $154.1 million. Rebuilding the series could remove the eight-negative-years narrative and select a different anchor or growth framework, reasonably changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every annual OE bridge from audited statements using correct annual XBRL contexts, signs, capex periods, drydocking treatment, and explicit non-operating adjustments; restore FY2023 and rerun the anchor, too-hard decision, growth cases, and valuation.

audit_findings.title: Interest income may be capitalized twice
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.144 million annual OE overstatement; computed value effect of $2.60-$4.06 per share, including $3.64 per share in the base case
audit_findings.mechanism: Interest income remains in anchor OE while the associated cash is separately added through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: Interest income amounted to $11.1 million for the year ended March 31, 2026, compared to $15.2 million for the year ended March 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The error is demonstrated: filed FY2026 net income of $193.666 million plus $71.744 million of D&A less $93.844 million of investing capex equals $171.566 million, effectively the supplied $171.5 million anchor, so no $11.144 million interest-income purge occurred. Applying the supplied scenario capitalization factors gives values of approximately $45.42 bear, $60.24 base, and $66.35 bull after removal. These remain on the same side of the $55.20 price as the original bear, base, and bull cases; the base correction is smaller than the original $8.68-per-share base premium, and the price remains above the buy-below threshold. It is therefore a real but not conclusion-changing error on the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Insert an explicit $11.144 million interest-income subtraction in the GAAP-to-OE bridge, separately review the $1.076 million investment-security gain and hedge settlements, and rerun all scenarios and the buy-below calculation.

audit_findings.title: Post-year-end vessel sale creates a numerator-perimeter mismatch
audit_findings.magnitude: $81.9 million filed net sale proceeds and $16.5 million debt prepayment; normalized Cobra earnings adjustment unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: FY2026 anchor OE includes earnings from Cobra while the June bridge includes post-sale cash and debt effects, potentially recognizing both the disposed asset's earnings stream and its proceeds.
audit_findings.evidence: On May 6, 2026, we completed the sale of this vessel, receiving proceeds net of commissions and fees of $81.9 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated, but the record does not disclose Cobra-specific normalized OE, so its valuation effect cannot be established. The sale proceeds themselves are not the error magnitude because they belong in the bridge; the possible overstatement is the capitalization of earnings that ceased with the sale. The subsequent dividend and the later Corsair and Constellation sales further require a consistent valuation-date perimeter, but their effects should not be folded into Cobra without a complete bridge.
audit_findings.action: Produce vessel-level normalized OE for Cobra, remove it from the anchor as of the disposal date, and reconcile the $81.9 million proceeds, $16.5 million debt prepayment, June cash, dividends, and all later vessel-sale cash and debt movements exactly once before rerunning the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Anchor mixes a full newbuilding outlay with almost no earnings from the vessel
audit_findings.magnitude: $85.706 million of filed FY2026 Areion installment payments, equal to 50.0% of the $171.5 million anchor; total filed vessel-construction and other vessel capex was $93.844 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Growth capex is deducted from anchor OE despite virtually no Areion operating contribution, and future growth is then charged again through the DCF's RONTA reinvestment mechanism.
audit_findings.evidence: For the year ended March 31, 2026, net cash used in investing activities was comprised of $93.8 million of payments for vessel under construction and other capital expenditures for vessels, including vessel upgrades.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated timing and classification error. Areion was delivered on March 20, 2026, while FY2026 included $85.706 million of construction installments and the anchor arithmetic deducted the full $93.844 million investing outlay. The identified Areion installments alone are half of reported anchor OE, large enough to change both intrinsic value and the buy decision. The final correction remains subject to separating true maintenance and upgrade spending from growth investment and adding normalized Areion earnings and financing costs consistently.
audit_findings.action: Classify the $93.844 million by Areion growth installments, construction costs, maintenance, upgrades, and other capex; remove growth capex from normalized OE, add normalized Areion earnings and interest, and rerun the DCF without duplicating reinvestment through RONTA.

audit_findings.title: Recurring drydocking cash may be omitted from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $16.985 million FY2026 omitted cash charge; computed value effect of $3.97-$6.19 per share, including $5.54 per share in the base case
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor adds back total D&A, including deferred-drydocking amortization, but deducts only investing capex and therefore leaves no economic charge for recurring drydocking cash.
audit_findings.evidence: We spend significant amounts for scheduled drydocking (including the cost of classification society surveys) for each of our vessels.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is demonstrated by the anchor arithmetic and cash-flow statement. FY2026 drydocking payments were $16.985 million, while $7.004 million of drydocking amortization was included in D&A and then fully added back. Capitalizing the omitted FY2026 cash charge would reduce the supplied base value from $63.88 to about $58.34 per share. Although that remains above the $55.20 price, it removes roughly 64% of the base-case premium and is reasonably capable of changing the practical valuation conclusion once drydocking is normalized across the fleet cycle.
audit_findings.action: Build a multi-year drydocking schedule by vessel, reconcile cash additions and amortization, select a normalized recurring maintenance charge, deduct it once in OE, and rerun every scenario and the buy-below value.

audit_findings.title: The latest positive year may be a cyclical-rate peak rather than durable OE
audit_findings.mechanism: A potentially above-cycle TCE level enters anchor OE and is compounded through explicit growth and a terminal value representing about half of scenario value.
audit_findings.evidence: The spot market is very volatile and there have been and will be periods when spot charter rates decline below the operating cost of vessels.
audit_findings.explanation: This is an unresolved normalization risk, not a demonstrated accounting error. Filed TCE rates show substantial cyclicality: $62,129 in FY2024, $39,778 in FY2025, $52,238 in FY2026, and $75,926 in the June 2026 quarter. Whether $171.5 million represents durable mid-cycle OE cannot be determined from the record. A computed 15.5% reduction in base operating value would eliminate the base case's premium to the $55.20 market price, which is well within the scale of the filed TCE fluctuations; the issue is therefore reasonably capable of changing the conclusion despite its unquantified normalized amount.
audit_findings.action: Construct a full-cycle normalization using filed TCE, utilization, bunker, operating-cost, charter-in, and fleet-perimeter data; stress the anchor directly at mid-cycle and trough rates and rerun the DCF and terminal-value share.
